seats: secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: Wisdom as a person: she calls out, builds her house, is called “my sister”; “the wisdom of God said”
fixes.why: “As a person” states as fact what the verses do as a figure (a woman addressed as sister, wisdom “vindicated by her actions”). The note itself says readers part on whether this is a person, an attribute or a figure of speech, so the label settles the question the note leaves open. Scholars name this personification.
fixes.fix: Relabel: “Wisdom spoken of as a woman: she calls out, builds her house, is called ‘my sister’; ‘the wisdom of God said’”. Keep the note. The note's three repeats of “the page does not choose” can be cut to one.

fixes.row: ROW ORDER, noun form: Jesus and wisdom is the second row
fixes.why: Rule 2 forbids a row order that settles a question. Placing Jesus-and-wisdom directly under Wisdom-personified, and before the fear of the LORD, Solomon, Job and Ecclesiastes, reads as a staircase to “Christ is the Wisdom of Proverbs 8”, the very point the notes say readers dispute. It is also a later reading placed ahead of the earlier text. The story's own arc (fear of the LORD, Wisdom's call, God's wisdom in creation, Solomon, Job's question, Ecclesiastes' limits, the prophets' critique, Daniel, then the New Testament) is hidden.
fixes.fix: Reorder the noun form so the Old Testament rows come first and Jesus and wisdom follows them: fear of the LORD; get wisdom; wisdom personified; God's wisdom; the LORD gives; Spirit; skill; Solomon; Job; Ecclesiastes; folly/pride; nations and the prophets; Daniel; then Jesus and wisdom, placed directly beside the wisdom of men and ‘of this age’ (see next fix). Then the grab-bag rows (beside knowledge, mouth, every other use) last.

fixes.row: Jesus and wisdom / The wisdom of men and of the nations
fixes.why: 1 Cor 1:19-31 is one argument: Isa 29:14 quoted, the wisdom of the world made foolish (1:20), then Christ the wisdom of God (1:24, 1:30). The hub cuts it into two rows at opposite ends of the form, so the arc Paul draws from Isaiah to Christ is not visible.
fixes.fix: Keep both rows but adjacent, and add to each a note pointing to the other (“1 Cor 1:19-31 runs from the one to the other”), with no gloss on how they relate.

fixes.row: The wisdom of men and of the nations, “of this age”: boasted in, made foolish, brought to nothing, led astray
fixes.why: The label's quoted phrases (“of this age”, “made foolish”, “brought to nothing”) are Paul's. Fifteen of the 25 verses are Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Proverbs, which speak of Israel's own wise men, Edom, Tyre and Assyria on their own terms. They are filed under a New Testament heading. Prov 21:30 (“no wisdom … that can prevail against the LORD”) states a principle and is not about men's wisdom boasted in or made foolish.
fixes.fix: Split in two: (a) “The wisdom of the wise and of the nations: boasted in, led astray, to perish” (Isa, Jer, Ezek, Obad, Prov 21:30, Acts 7:22); (b) “The wisdom of the world, of this age” (1 Cor 1-3, 2 Cor 1:12, Jas 3:15). Put (b) beside Jesus and wisdom.

fixes.row: Wisdom set against folly, pride and the rod: “fools despise wisdom”; “with humility comes wisdom”
fixes.why: “Set against … the rod” misstates Prov 29:15: “A rod of correction imparts wisdom.” The verse joins the rod to wisdom, it does not oppose them. A reader skimming the label gets the opposite of the example. The row has no note.
fixes.fix: Relabel: “Wisdom and folly, pride, and correction: ‘fools despise wisdom’; ‘with humility comes wisdom’; ‘a rod of correction imparts wisdom’”.

fixes.row: Wisdom and the law: the statutes, the commandments, the precepts
fixes.why: The example shows “faithful instruction” on a woman's tongue. A reader sees neither statutes, commandments nor precepts, so the example does not show its label. The note admits the Berean prints ‘instruction’, and the verse is already in the mouth row.
fixes.fix: Move Prov 31:26 out (it stays in the mouth row), or relabel to “Wisdom and the law: statutes, precepts, laws, and ‘instruction’ (tora)”. Preferred: move it out.

fixes.row: Wisdom and the law: the statutes, the commandments, the precepts
fixes.why: The Old Testament's own link between Torah and becoming wise (Ps 19:7, “making wise the simple”; Ps 119:98) sits only in the one-row verb form, and Deut 4:6's “wise and understanding people” is parked in the adjective form's catch-all. The row holds four verses and the law-and-wisdom link is thin where it is strongest. 2 Tim 3:15 (the Holy Scriptures “able to make you wise”) is in the verb row far from it.
fixes.fix: Add a note to the law row listing Ps 19:7, Ps 119:98, Deut 4:6 (adjective) and 2 Tim 3:15 as “the same link in the verb and adjective forms”, or add them to the row with their word tags. No claim about law and the Christian.

fixes.row: Solomon's wisdom: given by God, asked for, heard of, beyond all the kings of the earth
fixes.why: Solomon's request and the LORD's answer in 1 Kgs 3 (“a wise and discerning heart”, 3:12) is in the adjective form's Called wise row, not here, so the noun row opens at the verdict (3:28) with the request cut away. The story is split by word form.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: “The request and the answer, 1 Kgs 3:5-14, use the adjective; see Called wise.”

fixes.row: Skilled: craftsmen and workers in every kind of work, the most skillful of the wailing women, captains, an expert builder
fixes.why: In the Berean, 2 Chr 2:12 reads “He has given King David a wise son with insight and understanding”, which is Solomon, not a craftsman. The Hebrew word for the craftsman Huram-abi is a verse number later in the Hebrew text, so the example does not show the label. Isa 3:3 (“the cunning magician, and the clever enchanter”) is a leader of Jerusalem, not a worker or craftsman.
fixes.fix: Move 2 Chr 2:12 to Called wise, with a note that the Berean's verse numbering is one off from the Hebrew; use 2 Chr 2:13 for Huram-abi. Move Isa 3:3 to the wise men and magicians row, or to Every other use.

fixes.row: Wisdom in the mouth, in teaching and in daily life: “the mouth of the righteous man utters wisdom”; “teach and admonish one another with all wisdom”
fixes.why: Several verses are not about speech or teaching. Prov 24:3 (“By wisdom a house is built”) belongs with the builders and Wisdom's house (Prov 9:1, Exod 31:3) and is the creation-and-tabernacle thread (Prov 3:19). Prov 14:8 is the prudent discerning his way; Eccl 8:1 is wisdom brightening a face; Prov 30:3 is Agur saying “I have not learned wisdom”. The row is a catch-all with no note and no door, and its label promises more than its content.
fixes.fix: Move Prov 24:3 to the Skill row with a note that it and Exod 31:3 and Prov 3:19 use the same three words (wisdom, understanding, knowledge); move Eccl 8:1 to Ecclesiastes; move Prov 14:8 and Prov 30:3 to Get wisdom or a new row “The way of wisdom” with Prov 4:11. Relabel what remains “Wisdom on the lips and in teaching” and add a one-line note.

fixes.row: Wisdom and the fear of the LORD
fixes.why: This is the book's thesis (Prov 1:7, 9:10; Job 28:28; Ps 111:10) and its framing statement, yet it is a six-verse row sixth from the top, after Jesus and Solomon. Its prominence is the Old Testament's own; the story begins here.
fixes.fix: Move to the first row of the noun form and keep the label (see ROW ORDER).

fixes.row: Wisdom beside knowledge, understanding, insight, instruction, discretion
fixes.why: At 62 verses it is a word-pairing list, not a statement of what the text says; almost every verse is already in another row, and it repeats the lists of Job 28, Prov 1-4 and Exod 31 without a statement. It also brings Rev 13:18 and 17:9 under ‘insight’, a different word, while Daniel's row holds them for ‘wisdom’. It is honest about this in the note, but a reader scanning for what wisdom is will meet it as the largest row.
fixes.fix: Keep it but move it to the end of the noun form with the label “Words that stand beside wisdom (a list; every verse is also in the rows above or below)”, so it reads as an index and not a claim.

fixes.row: The Spirit of God and wisdom: “filled with the Spirit of God, with skill”; “a spirit of wisdom”; “full of the Spirit and wisdom”
fixes.why: The door to ‘the Holy Spirit’ is attached to the whole row, including Exod 31:3, Deut 34:9 and Isa 11:2, which in their own place name the Spirit of God, the Spirit of the LORD, and ‘a spirit of wisdom’ given through Moses' hands. Offering the Christian divine-person node as the door to these verses reads a later doctrine back into them; the note does say readers part. Under Rule 3 the door is applied by row, not by hand per verse.
fixes.fix: Either keep the door only for the Acts and Eph/1 Cor verses (a second row “In the New Testament”) or relabel the door “the Spirit of God” for the Old Testament verses. Split the row into (a) Old Testament: Exod 28:3, 31:3, 35:31, Deut 34:9, Isa 11:2 and (b) New Testament: Acts 6:3, 6:10, Eph 1:17, 1 Cor 12:8.

fixes.row: The wise and the fool, the foolish, the simple, the mocker (adjective) and The wise in their own eyes … confounded (adjective)
fixes.why: Rule 7: the same verses (1 Cor 1:27, 3:18, 3:19, Isa 29:14, Jer 4:22, Prov 26:5) appear in the adjective rows ‘wise and fool’ and ‘wise in their own eyes’, and again in the noun row of the wisdom of men. At 26 rows the hub is over the brief's 25, and a reader will find the same sayings three times.
fixes.fix: Merge the adjective row ‘wise in their own eyes … confounded’ into the noun row of the wisdom of men and nations (split as above), or leave the verses in one place and list the others as ‘also here’.

fixes.row: Be wise, grow wise, make wise: “become wise”, “wiser than all men”, “make you wise for salvation”
fixes.why: Exod 1:10 (“deal shrewdly”, Pharaoh against Israel) is the verb's other sense; the label does not name it, so the example shows a plan to oppress under a heading of growing wise. The label quotes 2 Tim 3:15, a different Greek word (σοφίζω) than the Hebrew verbs in the other 26 verses, and puts the New Testament verse in the label though only 1 of 27 is New Testament. The row is a single catch-all.
fixes.fix: Relabel: “Be wise, grow wise, make wise; and the same verb for shrewd dealing (Exod 1:10)”. Move the 2 Tim 3:15 quotation out of the label and into the note; note that it is a different Greek verb.

fixes.why: The largest row in the hub is a bin. It holds Israel called “a wise and understanding people” (Deut 4:6), Rom 1:14 (“the wise and the foolish”, which fits the wise-and-fool row), and Deut 16:19 (a bribe blinds the wise). The label says nothing, so Rule 1 (a label says what its verses say) has nothing to check.
fixes.fix: Pull out two rows: “Israel and the people called wise” (Deut 4:6, Deut 32:6, Hos 14:9) and “The wise hear and learn” (Prov 1:5, 9:9, 12:15, 13:1). Move Rom 1:14 to the wise and fool row. Leave only a few verses in Every other use.

worker_points.point: 1. Row 1 and row 2, Wisdom personified; Prov 8:22-31 not listed; 8:22 and 8:30 quoted in the note
worker_points.why: Withholding the verdict and naming both sides is right, and the note's remark on “created” versus the word-by-word “possessed” is true (the Hebrew is q-n-h; I checked 8:22 in the Berean). Two fixes: the label ‘as a person’ decides the question; and the two rows are second to each other in the order, which suggests the answer. Luke 2:40, Matt 13:54 and Mark 6:2 should stay in the Jesus row as the worker had them; the note says which words the verse has.

worker_points.point: 2. Row 5, “a spirit of wisdom” and the Spirit
worker_points.why: The note is careful, but the door ‘the Holy Spirit’ and the single mixed row put the Old Testament verses under a divine-person heading; split by testament (see the OT framing fix). 1 Cor 12:8 is fine to keep.
Ezek 28 is kept as a lament “for the king of Tyre”, with the note that readers part; this is connect, not interpret. The row heading is the problem (OT framing), not these verses.

The shared words are ‘wisdom’ and ‘insight’ and the note keeps from saying what is to be understood. Note that Dan 12:10 (“the wise will understand”) uses שָׂכַל, which the hub holds in Other words; a one-line pointer from this row to it would help the Daniel-to-Revelation reader.
Both verses are quoted and the sentence names where each stands. A cross-pointer in each row would let the contrast show. Jas 3:13-18 is one passage.
The note about תורה is accurate and takes no side. Prov 31:26 does not show the label and the Torah-makes-wise verses (Ps 19:7, 119:98) are elsewhere (see the fixes).
This is the book's own tension; the note is the right height. Move Eccl 8:1 here from the mouth row.

worker_points.point: 8. Adjective, God is called wise (3 verses; Isa 31:2 left out)
worker_points.why: The verses name God. The note on Isa 31:2 says why “He” is not filled in. Leave as is.

The best handled point in the hub: the note says the Berean prints ‘skill’ and ‘wisdom’ for the same word and declines to say one meaning or two. Add Prov 24:3 and the shared triad with Exod 31:3 and Prov 3:19.

The label (“confounded, made foolish, put to shame, passed over”) pushes the verse toward a reading of selection, and the note says only “the page does not say more”, which reads as a hint. The row heading has to be corrected, not just the placement. Either state in the note that Matt 11:25 and Luke 10:21 are Jesus' thanksgiving to the Father, or let them stand in their own small row “Hidden from the wise and revealed to little children”.

missing.what: Prov 8:22-31 has no wisdom word in its own verses and is quoted only in a note. Add it as a span (verse range) attached to the personification row, shown without a word tag, so the heart of the Old Testament's wisdom passage is not absent from a hub on wisdom.

Genesis 3:6 (“desirable for obtaining wisdom”) and Solomon's request (1 Kgs 3) are the two ends of an Old Testament story about getting wisdom, but Gen 3:6 is held only in Other words (a different Hebrew word). A one-line pointer from the Get wisdom row to Other words would keep the different word apart and still show the story.

Job 28's answer and Proverbs 8-9's call are not tied: Job 28:12 and 28:20 ask where wisdom is found, and Prov 1:20 and 8:1 show wisdom calling out in the street. The two rows are far apart and the hub gives no pointer from one to the other.

examples_checked: Read the four examples of 18 of 26 rows in the hub text and 16 more verses in the Berean. 22 of 26 rows' examples show their label; the four that do not are Wisdom and the law (Prov 31:26 shows ‘instruction’ only), Skilled adjective (2 Chr 2:12 in the Berean is Solomon), the mouth row (Prov 24:3, 14:8, 30:3 and Eccl 8:1 are not about speech) and Wisdom set against folly, pride and the rod (Prov 29:15 says the rod imparts wisdom).
summary: The hub keeps close to the text, and its notes on Prov 8:22, skill/wisdom and Ecclesiastes are careful. It ships after fixes: the row order puts Jesus and wisdom straight after the personified Wisdom of Proverbs and ahead of the Old Testament rows, a label states a person, the Spirit and nations rows file Old Testament verses under New Testament headings, four rows have examples that do not show their label, and Prov 8:22-31 needs a span.
